desc: Natural light display in Arctic skies. Caused by solar particles colliding with atmosphere. Green, red, purple colors. Best seen near magnetic pole.

desc: Southern hemisphere counterpart to Northern Lights. Visible from Tasmania, NZ, Antarctica. Same solar particle mechanism.

desc: Sunlight refracted by water droplets. Full circle in ideal conditions. Primary bow: red outer, violet inner. Secondary bow has reversed colors. Alexander's dark band between bows.
fact: Sunlight + water droplets · Full circle · Primary/secondary bows · Alexander's band

desc: Sudden electrostatic discharge between clouds or cloud-ground. Heats air to 30,000°C. World's most lightning-prone area: Lake Maracaibo, Venezuela (Catatumbo lightning).
Seasonal reversal of winds bringing heavy rain. Indian summer monsoon (June-Sept) most famous. Caused by differential heating of land/ocean. Lifeblood for agriculture in South Asia.
fact: Seasonal wind reversal · Indian summer monsoon · June-Sept · Agriculture lifeblood

desc: Warming of central/eastern Pacific Ocean. Weakens trade winds. Triggers global weather disruptions: floods, droughts. Occurs every 2-7 years. Lasts 9-12 months.
fact: Pacific warming · Weak trade winds · Global disruptions · 2-7 year cycle

desc: Cooling of central/eastern Pacific. Strengthens trade winds. Opposite effects to El Niño. Often follows El Niño.
fact: Pacific cooling · Strong trade winds · Opposite of El Niño · ENSO cool phase

desc: Lightning produced in volcanic eruption plumes. Friction between ash particles creates static charge. Observed at Eyjafjallajökull, Vesuvius, Sakurajima.
fact: Volcanic plume · Ash particle friction · Static charge · Dirty thunderstorm

desc: Bright spots appearing beside the sun. Caused by ice crystals in cirrus clouds. Most visible when sun is low. Often associated with approaching weather systems.
fact: Bright spots beside sun · Ice crystals · Cirrus clouds · Low sun · Cold weather

desc: Enlarged shadow of observer projected onto cloud/mist below. Glowing halo (glory) around shadow's head. Named after Brocken peak in Germany. Common in mountains.
fact: Enlarged shadow on cloud · Glowing halo · Brocken, Germany · Mountain phenomenon
